$comment: SYNTHETIC (T-035, DL-148). The full production sysstats record with timespan one above the signed BIGINT maximum: 9223372036854775808 is 9223372036854775807 + 1 and is NINETEEN digits, so it passes the schema's ^(0|[1-9][0-9]{0,18})$ pattern and the record is SCHEMA-VALID - which is why it lives in valid/. sysstats is the one type where timespan is a STRING on the wire ("300" where every other type sends an integer, ADR-007 s6), so the Writer parses the digit string and, exactly as LorastatsDialects does for its string counters, range-checks it against BigInteger BEFORE any narrowing conversion (DL-105 rule 3, STA-04C). The gap between nineteen digits and the BIGINT maximum is not expressible as a regex, so this line can only be held by the Writer. The record dead-letters as unmappable on its first attempt; nothing is written, nothing is zeroed, nothing is truncated. $expect is writer-range-reject rather than writer-dlq because the record does NOT fail its per-type schema.
